newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: France has not asked Italy for stronger lira - Prodi. [CORRECTED 07:45 GMT 6/10]
newsitem.headline: France has not asked Italy for stronger lira - Prodi. [CORRECTED 07:45 GMT 6/10]

text.p: The French government has not asked Italy to encourage a further appreciation in the lira before seeking the currency's re-entry into Europe's Exchange Rate Mechanism, Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Saturday. (Corrects Prodi's title from president).
Speaking to Reuters Financial Television after an informal summit of EU leaders, Prodi said, "They did not ask for a revaluation."
French president Jacques Chirac met Prodi on Friday to discuss, among other things, Italy's return to the ERM, a step Rome wants to take as soon as possible.
France has argued in the past that for the lira to re-enter the currency grid a further appreciation would be necessary.
Prodi said the lira's return would be a multi-lateral decision, involving all of the EU's 15 nations.
Regarding the chances of Italy and Spain joining the first wave of countries in a single currency in 1999, Prodi said, "We have no less chance than Spain to get in."
